keyword: what eye drops are being recalled
claims: Over 3.1 million bottles of over-the-counter eye drops manufactured by K.C. Pharmaceuticals are being recalled due to concerns over a lack of sterility assurance.
The recalled products could cause temporary, reversible eye infections.
The recalled products were sold at CVS, Walgreens, Rite Aid, Walmart, H-E-B, and Kroger.

Recalled products and brands include Dry Eye Relief Eye Drops, Artificial Tears Sterile Lubricant Eye Drops, Advanced Relief Eye Drops, Redness Lubricant Drops, Sterile Eye Drops (various types: AC, Original Formula, Soothing Tears).
Store brands involved include CVS Health, Walgreens, Rite Aid, Equaline, Leader, H-E-B, Kroger, Best Choice, Quality Choice, Meijer, and Dollar General.
K.C. Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is the manufacturer.
K.C. Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is located in Pomona, California.
Class II means the product may cause temporary or reversible adverse health consequences.
Many affected products have expiration dates between May 2026 and October 2026.
The FDA has a full list of NDC or UPC numbers for the recalled products.
This information is based on reports as of early April 2026.
